name: Outgoing webhooks
needs: let my users get notified in Zapier when something happens
send an event to a customer's URL
customers want a callback when a job finishes
my webhook calls fail and nobody retries them
summary: Your app calls a URL your user gave you each time an event happens, like order.paid or report.ready. Done right, every delivery is signed, saved, retried with backoff and visible in a log, so a customer's slow server can't slow you down.
need_when: Users want other tools (Zapier, Make, n8n, their own code) to react to events in your app.
Customers keep polling your API to ask if something changed.
skip_when: No user has asked for integrations yet. A CSV export or email may be enough for now.

ways.title: A deliveries table and your own worker
ways.how: Save one row per (endpoint, event) when the event happens. A background worker sends it, records the response code and schedules a retry on failure.
ways.tradeoff: Full control and no vendor. You build the retry schedule, signing, logs and the customer-facing settings page yourself.

ways.title: A webhook delivery service
ways.how: Svix or Hookdeck take your events and handle signing, retries, logs and an endpoint portal you can embed.
ways.tradeoff: Saves weeks. Another vendor sees your event payloads and bills per message at volume.

ways.title: Queue plus a serverless sender
ways.how: Push events to a queue (SQS, Cloudflare Queues) and let a function deliver them with the queue's retry and dead-letter settings.
ways.tradeoff: Scales well. Per-endpoint logs and a replay button are still yours to build.

prompt:
Add outgoing webhooks so users can subscribe a URL to events in my app.

Requirements:
- Users can add an endpoint (HTTPS only), pick which events it gets, and see its signing secret once.
- When an event happens, save a delivery row per endpoint in the same database transaction as the change. A background worker sends it.
- Body is JSON with id, type, created timestamp and data. Sign the timestamp plus body with HMAC-SHA256 and send the signature, timestamp and event id as headers.
- 10 second timeout. Don't follow redirects. Treat any 2xx as success.
- Retry failures with exponential backoff and jitter for about [8] attempts over a day, then mark the delivery dead.
- Block destinations that resolve to private, loopback or link-local addresses.
- Give users a delivery log (time, event, status code, attempt count) and a "resend" button.
- Disable an endpoint after [N] days of only failures and email its owner.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. A receiver can verify the signature with the secret and a 10-line script.
2. Pointing an endpoint at a server that returns 500 shows retries spreading out in the log.
3. An endpoint at http://127.0.0.1 or a private IP is rejected.
4. A receiver that sleeps 60 seconds does not hold up other deliveries.
5. Resending a delivery uses the same event id, so receivers can drop the duplicate.
acceptance_checks: A receiver can verify the signature with the secret and a 10-line script.
Pointing an endpoint at a server that returns 500 shows retries spreading out in the log.
An endpoint at http://127.0.0.1 or a private IP is rejected.
A receiver that sleeps 60 seconds does not hold up other deliveries.
Resending a delivery uses the same event id, so receivers can drop the duplicate.
if_you_skip_it: Customers miss events whenever their server blips, nobody can tell what was sent, or your server gets used to probe internal addresses.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal can send webhooks to URLs its users register. Each delivery is a saved row that a webhook worker sends with HMAC-SHA256 signatures, an event id that doubles as an Idempotency-Key header and a 10 second timeout. Failures retry with jittered backoff starting at 30 seconds and capped at 6 hours, for up to 8 attempts, then the delivery is marked dead. Destinations must be HTTPS, redirects aren't followed and private addresses are blocked.
